scope: Actual visual inspection with view_image of all seven newly extracted corrected capture frames, not inherited approval of the earlier candidate. Game files were not modified and no GPU process was launched for this review.

source_videos.scope: actual production weapon events in a controlled capture; no live-frame-rate claim
actual production weapon events in a controlled capture; no live-frame-rate claim

frames.review: Actual muzzle discharge is unobstructed: irregular warm flame tongues project ahead of the barrel, with a brief local ground light. The tank remains readable; no opaque explosion sphere or rectangular smoke-card edge is visible.

The collision-triggered close view shows a bright broken flame cluster, airborne building fragments and gold streaks radiating at different angles from the actual hit. The former parallel horizontal streak defect is absent.

Strongest damage/effect evidence: elongated sparks follow outward trajectories at visibly different angles; tumbling fragments, patchy fire and transparent dust leave the destroyed centre and surviving building readable. No directional scaling defect is visible.

The initial fire has ended. Thin textured grey/cream smoke has soft alpha edges; decaying sparks and fragments remain visible and the destroyed centre is exposed. No opaque orb or rectangular fringe hides the damage.

The complete fighter is visible against the harbour. The bright projectile ahead of the nose is now inclined along its projected travel direction rather than stretched horizontally. This is a launch view, not an impact view.
Compared with frame31 the projectile has advanced toward the distant city while retaining alignment with its trajectory. Aircraft silhouette and wing/tail components remain unobstructed.

The repeated launch after frame55 again produces a forward-aligned bright projectile. The fighter is readable without visible missing geometry or foreground occlusion. The projectile is intentionally small in this landscape shot.

limitations: The aerial clip demonstrates launch visibility and corrected projectile orientation, not missile impact; collision/damage is covered by the separate native combat QA.
The cinematic capture uses controlled simulation and camera framing and is not a performance benchmark.
The source capture clips are identified separately from the exported App; the App combat report independently passed 42 checks.
